# Temple Scroll Column 43 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 43 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 43:1 — "creatures that go on all fours" vs. "four-footed creatures" vs. "four-footed creature with paws" — phrasing

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "all creatures that go on all fours" | Literal Hebrew syntax |
| LOGOS | "all four-footed creatures" | Compressed formal |
| PNEUMA | "any four-footed creature with paws" | Expanded for clarity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET phrasing for literal fidelity to the Hebrew idiom.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 43:4 — "mouse" vs. "mouse" vs. "rat" — akhbar identification

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the mouse" | Traditional rendering |
| LOGOS | "the mouse" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "the rat" | Modern equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "the mouse" per EMET and LOGOS. The Hebrew akhbar likely covers various rodents; "mouse" is the traditional translation.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 43:5 — "land crocodile" vs. "monitor lizard" vs. "monitor lizard" — koach identification

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the land crocodile" | Traditional KJV rendering |
| LOGOS | "the monitor lizard" | Modern zoological consensus |
| PNEUMA | "the monitor lizard" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "monitor lizard" per LOGOS and PNEUMA majority. Modern identification is more accurate than the archaic "land crocodile."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/PNEUMA.

---

## 43:11 — "detestable" vs. "abomination" vs. "disgusting" — sheqetz rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "detestable" | Standard project rendering |
| LOGOS | "an abomination" | Elevated formal term |
| PNEUMA | "disgusting" | Visceral modern term |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "detestable" per EMET. Consistent with established project rendering.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 43:14 — "sanctify yourselves" vs. "consecrate yourselves" vs. "set yourselves apart" — qiddesh rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "you shall sanctify yourselves" | Standard project rendering |
| LOGOS | "you shall consecrate yourselves" | Formal liturgical synonym |
| PNEUMA | "set yourselves apart" | Dynamic meaning-based |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "sanctify" per EMET and project convention.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 43:16 — "brought you up" vs. "brought you up" vs. "brought you out" — exodus verb

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "brought you up" | Literal he'elah — upward movement |
| LOGOS | "brought you up" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "brought you out" | Dynamic — focuses on departure |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "brought you up" per EMET and LOGOS. The Hebrew he'elah emphasizes ascent, which is theologically significant.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---
